## A safer way to understand disk usage

unused-removal is a native desktop scanner that shows large files, explains why each item was found, and leaves deletion decisions to you. It runs inside a private desktop protocol without opening a localhost server or TCP port.

![unused-removal Windows demo](https://github.com/inajaf/unused-removal/releases/download/v1.0.0/unused-removal-windows-demo.gif)

### Highlights

- Complete selected-drive or selected-folder scanning on Windows and macOS.
- Large and huge files are always surfaced for review.
- Clear **Safe**, **Review**, and **Protected** risk labels.
- Protected system paths remain visible but cannot be selected for deletion.
- Live scan and analysis progress; 100% is shown only when results are ready.
- Recycle Bin/Trash is the default recoverable cleanup path.
- English and Russian interface with a persistent RU/EN switch.
- Native desktop shell with no browser tab, localhost listener, or open port.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` contains checksums for every uploaded package and presentation asset.

### Installation notice

These community builds are not currently signed with a commercial Windows certificate or notarized with an Apple Developer ID. Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper may therefore show a warning. On macOS, use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** only after verifying the SHA-256 checksum.

### Competitive positioning

The included comparison image positions unused-removal as a guided review workflow: **scan → explain → review → Recycle Bin**. WinDirStat and TreeSize are primarily disk-usage analyzers, while BleachBit is primarily a rule-driven junk/privacy cleaner. See `marketing/README.md` in the source repository for the official product sources used in the comparison.
